title: TC-E2E-005: five identical execution requests produce exactly one effect (approved sandbox)
risk: A retried or redelivered action charges, ships or messages the customer twice because duplicate suppression relied on a cached response instead of a durable effect key.
preconditions: run_id=RUN-E2E-LIVE-IDEM, case_id=E2E-LIVE-IDEM, worker=w-biz-e2e-live; one approved sandbox recipient and a sandbox request_id taken from the inbound sandbox event are used, so the effect_key is reproducible across attempts
the sandbox provider account is a dedicated test account whose message/order count can be read back through the approved sandbox API

inputs.effect_key: deterministic key over (tenant, skill, step, revision, request_id)

steps.action: Submit the identical sandbox request five times
steps.expected: one sandbox dispatch is observed and the remaining submissions return the stored receipt (REPLAY/IN_FLIGHT) without provider calls

steps.action: Read the effect count back from the sandbox provider
steps.expected: the sandbox provider reports exactly one message/order for the effect_key and its id matches the receipt the engine returned

steps.action: Replay after a forced sandbox worker restart
steps.expected: the recomputed effect_key is identical and the reservation is found before any dispatch, so the outcome is RECONCILE_REQUIRED
the sandbox lookup confirms the effect exists, the reservation settles once and no second provider call is made

steps.action: Probe the collision path on the sandbox
steps.expected: the differing payload under the same effect_key is rejected with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and the sandbox provider test sink records no call for it — the provider test sink is the oracle for every denied or refused step: its call log for the run stays empty, no provider id is manufactured for the attempt, and the audit entry records the refusal instead
the live audit trail separates the single successful attempt from every duplicate attempt and duplicate-execution metrics for the run are 0

assertions: the sandbox provider holds exactly one external effect for the effect_key after five submissions, a restart and a replay
every duplicate submission resolves from the reservation path, with the provider message id returned by the engine matching the sandbox record

the collision attempt produced zero sandbox provider calls and a recorded IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT — a denied action has no provider receipt to show: the case records the decision, the zero-call sink and the audit entry, and never presents a receipt, order id or message id the provider did not return
the live audit trail names each attempt with its outcome and never reports a success for an attempt the sandbox did not confirm
forbidden: issuing a second sandbox message or order for the same effect_key
claiming idempotency from the cache response while the provider record shows a second effect
evidence: sandbox provider message/order record for the effect_key (exactly one)
sandbox reservation history plus the reconciliation lookup result
provider test-sink call log for the collision attempt (zero calls, retained)
cleanup: Retire the sandbox artefacts created by this run through the supported sandbox APIs (cancel/withdraw the created cart, campaign, case and voucher references); delete nothing immutable — sent messages, provider receipts and audit rows are retained and reported as non-deletable rather than pretending they were unsent
automation: Real code under test: skill registry row, authority guard/PEP, input validator, deadline and retry loop, effect_key reservation + reconciliation, evidence/audit writer. Substituted boundary: the external adapter (in-memory for offline, approved sandbox for live). Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; all waits are condition/deadline waits on the engine's virtual clock, never sleep. Same components on the sandbox; the sandbox provider transcript and its duplicate detection are the oracle.
prerequisites: ASM-001 approved connector lock is present (LIVE_CONNECTORS_LOCK points at the approved connector list) — without it this case is SKIP_ASM_001, never PASS

Per-case sandbox authorization: the run_id of this case is registered in the approved sandbox allowlist with its sandbox tenant/customer/SKU mapping before execution; credentials live outside the repository (env.local) and are never printed in evidence
The sandbox connector exposes a duplicate-detection or lookup-by-effect_key facility so the effect count can be observed; without it the case is BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE
